descriptionChirho: To utter words in direct or indirect speech, conveying a message or statement to someone — the primary and overwhelmingly common sense of λέγω covering all active voice inflections.
To issue a directive or instruction with authoritative force, where the speech act itself constitutes a command rather than mere communication of information.
To assign or bear a name or title, typically in passive or middle voice constructions meaning 'to be called' or 'to be known as' — a naming or designating function distinct from ordinary speech.
To speak or declare in a more formal or public sense, emphasizing the act of speaking itself or the authority of the discourse rather than the content of what is said.
Passive participle usage referring to the content or substance of what has been said or spoken, focusing on the words or message as a received or transmitted object.
